CV-04.c01: The **lower fifth wheel** is the coupling plate on the tractor; the **upper fifth wheel** (glide plate) is the flat plate under the trailer's front.
The **kingpin** has a base, a **shank**, and a head from top to bottom.
**Shut-off valves** sit in the service and supply lines at the rear of any trailer that pulls another trailer.
To **charge the trailer air system**, let air pressure rise to normal, then push the red air supply knob in.
CV-04.c02: Inspect a combination with the **same 7-step procedure** you learned in Section 2.
A combination has **more** of the usual parts to check, such as tires, wheels, lights, and reflectors, plus some **new** parts.
CV-04.c03: Lower fifth wheel → mounted firmly, greased, **no visible gap** between plates, and jaws closed around the kingpin **shank**, never its head.
Release arm seated with the **safety latch** engaged; upper fifth wheel's glide plate firmly mounted and kingpin undamaged.
Electrical cord secured; air lines coupled, not leaking, with **enough slack for turns** so they are not pulled apart.
Sliding fifth wheel → greased, **every locking pin** there and locked, not so far forward that the tractor frame hits the landing gear or cab hits the trailer.
Landing gear raised **all the way up**, undamaged, with the crank handle secured, because partly lowered gear can catch on railroad tracks.
CV-04.c04: Air-flow test → push knob in, apply trailer hand brake, then open the last trailer's **emergency** then **service** valves; air must come from both, then close them.
Shut-off valves stay **open**, except at the **rear of the last trailer**, which stay closed; no air at the rear means check they are open.
Tractor protection valve test → **engine off**, pump the brake pedal; the knob should pop out at the maker's pressure, **usually 20–45 psi** (not 25–40).
Emergency brakes → **pull out** the knob and tug gently; they should hold. Service brakes → roll slowly and apply the **hand valve**; feel them grab.
Leakage limits per minute, engine off → brakes released: **3 psi** (2 vehicles) or 5 psi (3 or more); foot brake held: **4 psi** or 6 psi.
